title: British Adventurer Finishes 28-Year Walk Around the World
paragraphs: After nearly three decades of walking, a British adventurer has finally completed his journey around the world on foot.

Karl Bushby, a former soldier from Hull in northeastern England, arrived at his mother's house on November 2, 2026, exactly "28 years and one day" after he set off. He was 29 years old when he began the journey in Punta Arenas, at the southern tip of Chile, in 1998, and he was 57 when he finished. Outside her home, he was welcomed with a hug by his mother, Angela.

Bushby's aim was to travel around the world without using any motorized transport and to return home only once he had completed the journey. Over the course of about 10,000 days, he covered roughly 50,000 kilometers and passed through 30 countries in South America, North America, Asia and Europe.

The journey turned out to be far longer than he had planned. Initially, he expected it to take about five years. However, he faced many obstacles along the way. In 2006, he crossed the frozen Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia, but he was detained after entering Russia illegally. In fact, Russia took him about a decade to cross, because harsh weather allowed him to walk for only a few months each year, and problems with paperwork repeatedly forced him to leave. After he was refused a Russian visa in 2012, he spent a year walking from Los Angeles to the Russian Embassy in Washington, DC, to obtain the documents he needed.

Later, when conflicts blocked his route through Russia and Iran, Bushby decided to cross the Caspian Sea, the world's largest inland body of water, instead. Using a flotation vest and a wetsuit, he took 31 days to cross it by a combination of floating and swimming. Before the final part of his walk home, he also swam across the English Channel.
Bushby admitted that he and his team had never imagined the journey would take 28 years. A documentary about his walk is now being made, and he plans to give talks around England.
